Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're navigating as a new mother, and I'm committed to supporting you through this journey. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool designed to help us understand your emotional well-being during the postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us valuable insights into how you're feeling and whether there's anything we can do to support you better.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm here to create a safe and non-judgmental space for you to express yourself. I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings with me, and I'm committed to listening with empathy and understanding.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of your emotional state over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and supportive as possible.

Let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love laughing and joking around, but since having the baby, it feels like that part of me has been kind of... muted. I do still laugh sometimes, like when my baby does something adorable, but it's not the same as it used to be. Most of the time, I just feel so overwhelmed and worried about taking care of her, and making sure she's healthy and safe. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is always "on" and worried about something, so it's hard for me to just relax and laugh like I used to. There are moments, though, when my husband or family will say something funny, and I'll laugh, but it feels a little forced, you know? Like I'm trying to be the person I used to be, but it's just not coming as naturally as it used to. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say that's been true for me, but to be honest, it's been a struggle. Like I said, I do laugh sometimes, but it's not as often as I used to, and it doesn't feel as genuine. I feel like I've lost a part of myself, you know? The baby is only a few weeks old, and I know I'm still adjusting, but it's hard not to feel like I'm just going through the motions sometimes. I look at my baby, and I love her so much, but I just feel so... tired and worried all the time. And when I do try to laugh or find the humor in something, it feels like it's just a distraction from all the things that are weighing on my mind. I don't know, maybe I'm just not giving myself enough time to adjust, but it's hard not to feel like something is missing right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll just feel too tired or overwhelmed to actually do it. Or, I'll worry about leaving the baby with someone else, even if it's just for a little while, and that worry will just suck the enjoyment out of it for me. I've also been feeling really guilty about taking time for myself, like I'm being a bad mom if I'm not constantly caring for the baby. It's hard to explain, but it's like my mind is always on the baby, and I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of myself, rather than actually enjoying things. Sometimes I'll think about things I used to look forward to, like trying a new restaurant or seeing friends, and I'll just feel sad because it feels like those things are so far out of reach right now. Does that make sense? It's like, I know I should be enjoying this time with my baby, but it's just so hard when I'm feeling so exhausted and anxious all the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I feel like I'm constantly second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right for the baby. If she's crying, I think it's because I'm not feeding her enough or changing her diaper often enough. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not creating a good bedtime routine. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. And it's not just the little things, either. I've been worrying that I'm not bonding with her like I should, or that I'm not producing enough milk for her. It's like, I know I'm trying my best, but it never feels like it's good enough. And that guilt and self-doubt just eats away at me. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding her or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed and inadequate. It's like, I know I'm supposed to be this confident, capable mom, but the truth is, I have no idea what I'm doing most of the time. And that feeling of uncertainty is just really hard for me to shake.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

All the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or watching her sleep, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she stops breathing? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if she gets sick? It's always something, and it's always worst-case scenario. And the thing is, I know it's irrational. I know that most of the time, everything is fine. But that doesn't stop my brain from going to these dark places. I'll be up at 3am, feeding her, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. It's like, my mind is just racing with all these what-ifs and maybes, and I just can't seem to calm myself down. Sometimes I'll try to distract myself by reading or watching TV, but even that doesn't always work. The anxiety just feels like it's always lurking, waiting to pounce. And it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, either. I worry about my relationship with my husband, and how we're going to manage as new parents. I worry about my own health, and whether I'm taking care of myself. It's just... everything, all the time. And it's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, everything is fine right now, but it won't be for long. And that's just a really hard way to live.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no reason for it. I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start feeling like I'm not in control, like everything is spiraling out of control. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my husband or family, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of panic. It's like, I know they're there to support me, but in that moment, I just feel so alone and scared. And the worst part is, I don't know how to make it stop. I'll try to breathe deeply, or distract myself, but sometimes it just takes over. I've had a few times where I've actually cried because I just felt so overwhelmed and scared. And it's not just the panic attacks, either. Sometimes I'll just feel this constant, low-level anxiety, like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong. It's exhausting, and it's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just living in a state of constant fear, like I'm always on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to keep up with my relationships... it all just feels so overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start feeling like I'm drowning in all the responsibilities. And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too, like laundry and dishes and meal prep. It all just feels so daunting, and I feel like I'm just not doing any of it well enough. I'll be up at 3am, feeding the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and I'll feel this wave of anxiety wash over me. It's like, I know I'm not alone, and I know my husband and family are there to support me, but it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough. And the guilt, oh the guilt... it's just crushing me. I feel like I'm not being a good enough mom, or a good enough wife, or a good enough person. It's like, I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but everything is just pulling me under.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie there and my mind will just start racing. I'll think about all the things I need to do, or worry about the baby's health, or just feel this overwhelming sadness. It's like, my brain won't turn off, and I just can't seem to relax. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so unsettling. I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge, and it's just hard to shake that feeling throughout the day. Sometimes I'll be so exhausted, but I just can't seem to wind down. I'll try to read a book or watch TV, but my mind will just keep wandering back to all the things that are worrying me. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the emotional toll it's taking on me. I feel like I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time, and it's hard to see a way out of it. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed and sad. It's like, I know I'm supposed to be happy and enjoying this time with my new baby, but the truth is, I'm just really struggling.
I have felt sad or miserable

.. that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so sad and overwhelmed all the time. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and trying to be a good mom, but inside, I'm just feeling so empty and miserable. I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so sad and overwhelmed. It's like, I know I'm supposed to be happy and enjoying this time with my new baby, but the truth is, I'm just really struggling. I feel like I've lost myself in all of this, like I'm just a mom now and not a person anymore. And it's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just living in a fog, like everything is just gray and dull and sad. I'll try to do things that I used to enjoy, like reading or watching TV, but nothing seems to bring me any joy anymore. It's like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really living. And it's hard to talk about, because I feel like I'm supposed to be grateful for this beautiful baby, and I am, but at the same time, I'm just so sad and overwhelmed. It's like, I'm torn between these two feelings, and I don't know how to reconcile them. Sometimes I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm finally turning a corner," but then the next day, I'll wake up and feel just as sad and miserable as before. It's just... it's really hard, you know.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It can be because of something specific, like the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, or it can be just out of nowhere. I'll be feeding her, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sadness and I'll start crying. It's like, I'm just so exhausted and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to keep going. Sometimes I'll cry because I'm just so frustrated, like I'm not doing anything right, and I'll just feel this wave of hopelessness wash over me. Other times, I'll cry because I'm just so sad, like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, and I don't know how to adjust to this new reality. It's like, I'll be looking at the baby, and I'll just feel so much love for her, but at the same time, I'll feel this overwhelming sadness, like I'm just not good enough for her. And it's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just crying all the time, like I'm just constantly on the verge of tears. Even when I'm not crying, I'll just feel this lump in my throat, like I'm just holding back tears all the time. It's like, I'm just so emotionally raw, and I don't know how to process all these feelings. Sometimes I'll try to talk to my husband about it, but even that can be hard, because I just feel so guilty, like I'm not being a good mom, or a good wife. It's just... it's really hard, you know.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices, such as establishing a consistent sleep schedule and creating a relaxing bedtime routine
3. Support the patient in developing a self-care plan, including activities that bring her joy and help her relax, such as reading, walking, or spending time with loved ones

5. Encourage the patient to reach out to her support network, including family and friends, for emotional support and help with childcare and household responsibilities
